assessment.security_status: Bezpečnostní situace v regionu se rapidně zostřuje po sérii útoků na klíčovou saúdskou ropnou infrastrukturu, uzavření ropovodu East-West a ofenzivě Húthíů podél pobřeží Rudého moře a dobytí strategického přístavu Mokha. US zprvu vedly tajná jednání s Húthíi o zajištění bezpečnosti amerických plavidel, což izoluje Saúdskou Arábii a zvyšuje riziko širšího regionálního konfliktu.

recommendations.reason: Přestože Húthíové uzavřeli tajnou dohody o neútočení na americká plavidla, celkové napětí a kontroly strategických koridorů (Mokha, Perim) udržují vysoké sazební prémie a rizika.

recommendations.sector: Obranný průmysl (např. RTX, Lockheed Martin, BAE Systems)
recommendations.reason: Saúdská Arábie čelí útokům dronů a raket na vlastním území (včetně Mekky) a urgentně poptává systémy protiraketové obrany, což zajistí silný přísun vládních zakázek.

recommendations.sector: Ropa a Plyn (např. Shell, BP, Chevron)
recommendations.reason: Vyřazení klíčového saúdského ropovodu (ztráta až 3,6 mil. barelů denně) spolu s útoky v Hormuzském průlivu a problémy v Panamském kanálu ženou ceny energonosičů prudce vzhůru.

recommendations.sector: Evropský Spotřební sektor & Autoprůmysl (např. Volvo, BMW)
recommendations.reason: Kombinace omezení v Panamském kanálu vinou sucha a nestability na Blízkém východě prodlužuje dodací lhůty komponent a zvyšuje fixní náklady na logistiku.

assessment.forecast: V nejbližších dnech lze očekávat další eskalaci ze strany Saúdské Arábie, která zůstává bez přímé vojenské podpory USA. To udrží ceny ropy na vysokých úrovních a přinese zvýšenou volatilitu na akciových trzích.

articles.title: Battle of Chile director Patricio Guzmán dies aged 85
articles.summary:
Passionate documentary maker won international acclaim for unsparing but poetic films exploring the impact of the Pinochet regime in Chile

Patricio Guzmán, the film-maker who chronicled Chile’s bloody 1970s political strife and its subsequent social and political turmoil in films such as The Battle of Chile and Nostalgia for the Light, has died aged 85. According to Chilean news outlet Emol, Guzmán died on Tuesday in Paris after a cardiorespiratory arrest.

Guzmán’s chief preoccupation throughout his career was the carnage unleashed by Augusto Pinochet’s coup in 1973 against Salvador Allende, Chile’s elected president. He later told the Guardian: “I’m a film-maker who was very marked by the ways of the dictator. It has remained with me for ever. I cannot leave it behind.” However, he resisted the idea that he was an activist, political film-maker, adding: “I’m not a sociologist. Neither am I a politician. I make films that are metaphorical and poetic; I interpret reality through my own personal way of looking.”

articles.title: Panama canal traffic facing further cuts as drought from El Niño worsens
articles.summary:
Planned daily reductions will further choke one of the world’s most important shipping lanes

The Panama canal plans to again cut maritime traffic due to worsening drought caused by the El Niño climate phenomenon, further choking up one of the world’s most important shipping lanes.

The canal handles 5% of global maritime trade and about 40% of US container traffic; it is favoured by shippers because it usually reduces cost and transit times, especially for companies trading between China, Asia and the US.

articles.title: Thursday briefing: Yemen’s war continues to threaten oil supplies– but what about its people?
articles.summary:
In today’s newsletter: The Houthi advance along the Red Sea coast raised fears for global trade and energy supplies, while more than 100,000 Yemenis have been displaced by the fighting

Good morning. The lightning advance of Houthi militants along the west coast of Yemen over the past week has prompted fears of a spiralling conflict in the region and a new oil supply crisis.

For families living in the Middle East’s poorest country, the most significant fighting between the Iran-aligned Houthis and the Saudi-backed Yemeni government forces in years is a crisis upon a catastrophe, with escalating civilian casualties and at least 100,000 displaced in recent days.

articles.title: US opts not to back Saudi Arabia in Yemen after meeting Houthi leaders
articles.summary:
Iran-backed militants have offered Trump administration assurances over safety of Red Sea shipping

Officials from the US met Houthi leaders over the weekend at the country’s embassy in Muscat, Oman, it has been confirmed, leading to the US decision not to intervene to help Saudi Arabia drive back a Houthi advance inside Yemen.

The Iran-backed militant group reassured the US that the ceasefire agreement between the two sides struck in 2025 still held and the movement had no intention of attacking US shipping in the Red Sea. Only Saudi-linked shipping was regarded as a target owing to its blockade of Yemen, the Houthis confirmed.

articles.title: 'Few cards to play': Saudi Arabia faces limited options against Houthis with allies out
articles.summary:
'Few cards to play': Saudi Arabia faces limited options against Houthis with allies out

For months, Saudi Arabia appeared fairly insulated from the war on Iran even as it engulfed smaller neighbours.

In fact, Saudi Aramco, the kingdom’s oil company, chalked up bumper profits this summer thanks to its East-West Pipeline, allowing crude exports to bypass the Strait of Hormuz.

Now, the East-West Pipeline is disabled because of a drone attack from Iran-aligned militias in Iraq. Houthi missiles and drones are hitting Saudi Arabian cities. A Houthi drone was even shot down over Mecca, the holiest city in Islam, whose custodianship is a point of legitimacy for the House of Saud. The Houthis have denied targeting Mecca.

Saudi Arabia now faces a two-front war.
